name: ashes

attributes.attribute: thrown at unmarried people on Ash Wednesday
used to bless cattle, fields, and people

sources: Danaher, Kevin. *The Year in Ireland.* Cork: Mercier Press, 1922. Pp. 50, 135.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Remnant ash from peat fires played a role in Irish folk tradition. Some traditions come from Christianity. Ash Wednesday begins the penitential season of Lent. People threw ashes at unmarried people then. This gave rise to a saying. The saying said a person would get the ash-bag thrown at them. The phrase meant the person was unmarriageable. Older traditions are probably pre-Christian. They used ashes as a Midsummer fertility symbol. The Lenten rite may have grown from this custom. People used ashes from Lughnasa bonfires to bless cattle. They also blessed fields and people with these ashes.

key_results: Document ashes as a symbolic material in Irish folk tradition.
Record the Ash Wednesday and Lenten association.
Note the pre-Christian Midsummer and Lughnasa uses.
